plain_what: Gives each token a long bit string (4,096 bits). XOR glues two things together, such as a role and a word. A majority vote merges many strings into one summary. Counting differing bits measures similarity. In the older prose model this added a cheap 'was this word recently in context' cue to the next-word score.
how_it_works: A hypervector is D = 4096 bits. Binding is bitwise XOR, which is its own inverse, so (A xor B) xor B = A. Permutation is a cyclic bit rotation, used to mark order. Bundling is a bitwise majority vote over a context window of up to 64 transition terms, with a fixed tie-breaker. Similarity is the Hamming distance from popcount, turned into a Q1.15 fixed-point bipolar correlation. Unbinding a bundle with a key gives a noisy copy of the stored value. For k random bipolar terms the cross-talk standard deviation grows as sqrt((k-1)/D), so 64 terms in 4096 bits leave a signal-to-noise ratio near 8. In the September prose scorer the term enters as one additive feature per candidate token: (vsa_scale_q15 * correlation(context_vec, code(candidate))) >> 16, where the context vector bundles an associative transition context and up to four 'orthogonal VSA attention' heads. Token codes have three modes: fixed hash (splitmix64 of seed and token id, expected distance D/2, so only identity carries signal), root (a hash of the token's icosian root, at most 120 distinct codes) and learned (root XOR a hash of a 5-D S2 readout, 4,096 distinct codes). The scale is trained; the codes are not. A separate router geometry switch used VSA facet stores for entity, relation and temporal retrieval.
geometry: The Hamming cube {0,1}^4096 with its XOR group and cyclic-shift automorphism; icosian roots (H4 120-root labels) as a code source in mode 1; the S2 readout in mode 2; the Fano-plane octonion table as a design-stage signed binding.

status_reason: Fixed-code VSA trained into the legacy native prose learner improved held-out BPB by 0.014-0.023 on 2 seeds and 2 slices, but the run used the CPU learner (barred by D24), and root codes, the mode-2 variant, frozen-artifact swaps and the router switch all failed or were uninformative (docs/labs/vsa-native-test-2026-10-09, vsa-review-2026-10-09). It is not on the D32 path.
reopen_conditions: A GPU-only, D23/D25-compliant retraining of the fixed-code term, either in an offline D37 float learner with a fresh FIT and a D11 integer export gap, or as a discrete Hamming binding on the D32 writer, with owner release where a hold applies.
The one follow-up the 9 Oct result justifies: freeze the mode-2 codebook after a warm-up and train on, to test the moving-codes hypothesis.
A redundancy test with the exact copy head ablated, plus a scale sweep (0, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000) on the artifact, so a null cannot be blamed on a tiny scale or on duplicated evidence.
A role-times-filler binding test on held-out phrasing against an equal-bit ordinary codebook, reporting decision-flip rate, with exact token and occurrence identity kept separate from the sketch.
For octonion-signed binding: a signed-XOR versus plain-XOR equal-cost test on order-sensitive relations using the canonical v63 Fano table, not the rejected draft table.

rule_compat.D11: Core ops (XOR, rotate, majority, popcount) are multiplier-free integer operations. The scorer's Q15 scale multiply ((scale * corr) >> 16) is a runtime product that has not been shown to be table-only, and serving always rebuilds the fixed hash codebook on demand. Not audited against the zero-multiply contract for any current path.
rule_compat.D23: The VSA operations contain no softmax or squashing. The host learner that trained the scale was not audited against D23 here (UNVERIFIED).
rule_compat.D30: Bitwise operations and popcount only; no matmul in the VSA algebra itself. The surrounding JEPA scorer was not audited.
rule_compat.D32_D37: D32 explicitly welcomes XOR and Hamming comparisons on ternary and E8 labels, with Hamming as one component, not a Hamming-only model (owner clarification 13 Oct). Binary 4096-bit hypervector VSA is not part of the D32 path, and the 9 Oct retraining ran on CPU (the record itself says it should have run elsewhere, owner rule #2095), so it breaks D24 as now written.

failed_only_on_configuration: Router geometry switch returning 0.0000 MRR (#434): a wiring defect in corpus ingestion, nothing about hypervectors.
8 Oct frozen-artifact code swaps (#820): the scale and other weights never co-adapted with the new codes, so they test inertness of a frozen term, not what VSA could contribute.
Root codes (mode 1): 120 codes for 4,096 tokens collapse token identity; says nothing about codes that keep identity and add structure.
Mode 2: the codebook was rebuilt from the readout every 1,000 steps while the heads trained, a plausible moving-target cause that was not tested.
#1284 'VSA attention inert': the codebook was inconsistent with the learned representation (D2), explicitly not a retirement verdict.
Draft octonion table: a sign-orientation defect in that table, not in octonion binding.
open_questions: Can codes derived from learned geometry (not a hash) keep identity and add similarity, and does that beat fixed hash codes? Mode 2 was the first attempt and lost.
Does the +0.014 to +0.023 BPB survive once the exact copy and prime-route heads already supply the same recency evidence at larger scale?
Is the engram table, not VSA, doing the real memory work? Removing it costs about 0.19-0.20 BPB against VSA's 0.013-0.016.
Would a bundle of about 64 terms in 4,096 bits carry order and bindings through unbinding, or only membership?
Does serving ignore the code mode? The review notes runtime.rs rebuilds the fixed codebook on demand, and ablate-prose prints a stale 'MIS-WIRED' label.

related.how: Same XOR, popcount and Hamming arithmetic; D32 favours it on ternary and E8 labels, so a discrete VSA would live there.
The intended partner: VSA sketches propose candidates and exact references decide the copied content.
Mode 1 derives codes from icosian roots; the result was that root-only codes collapse identity.
Both try to make a read bind the right value; VSA role-times-filler is the multiplier-free route to the same goal.
Its Hamming-on-coordinates distance is the discrete cousin of VSA similarity.
Both appear in the old 'prime and Hopf routing' stack as lossy summaries kept beside exact identity.
Supplies the Fano table used as the control for octonion-signed binding.

figure_ideas: Bind, bundle and probe on bit strips. Show three tokens as 64-cell bit strips, XOR each with a role strip, then fold them into one majority-vote strip. Pick a role and unbind: the matching token's strip lights up with a similarity bar, while noise bars for the others grow as more items are bundled (signal-to-noise near 8 at 64 items in 4,096 bits). (Static art already exists at docs/figures/geometry/vsa-hypervectors.svg to animate.)

Three code modes side by side on 4,096 token dots. Mode 0 (random hash): every dot far from every other. Mode 1 (root codes): dots collapse into 120 clumps. Mode 2 (root plus residual): clumps loosen. Beside each, the held-out BPB change against VSA off (-0.0144 to -0.0226, about 0, +0.013 to +0.028 worse than fixed).

A paired on/off ablation: for each of the two seeds and two slices, a pair of bars for BPB with the VSA term trained in and off, with the 0.01 bar drawn, so the viewer sees all four pairs clear it while the root-code bars do not.
